hook: Ummadisetti has been building production generative AI systems, RAG pipelines, model fine-tuning, agentic platforms, since before the term agentic AI entered general use. At Toyota North America he leads the function responsible for autonomous AI agents in one of the world's largest automotive manufacturers, while his seat on the LangChain advisory board gives him direct influence on the open-source tooling that most agentic systems are built on.
name: Ravi Chandu Ummadisetti

quote.text: Building GEN AI for Real-World Problems.

moniker: Head of Agentic AI at Toyota North America

reading.body:
Ravi Chandu Ummadisetti holds an unusual combination of positions: he runs the agentic AI function at Toyota North America and simultaneously sits on the advisory board of LangChain, the open-source framework most agentic systems are built on.

That dual position means he shapes both the industrial deployment of autonomous AI agents and the tooling layer that developers outside Toyota use to build them. His career path, from data analyst at Virtusa across banking, telecom, and healthcare, through a machine learning role at Santander Global Tech, to leading agentic AI at a top-three global automaker, tracks the maturation of applied ML into production generative AI. The data records no gap between his arrival at Toyota in 2022 and his LangChain board seat in 2026, which suggests the advisory role followed from his deployment experience rather than preceding it.

The data does not specify how many autonomous agents Toyota has in production, what compute infrastructure they run on, or how LangChain's architecture intersects with Toyota's internal systems. His patent covers automated meeting minutes, a narrower application than his current work, and the data does not connect it to his agentic AI mandate. What the record does establish is a practitioner who has moved generative AI through the full cycle, from experimental ML to enterprise deployment, in industries where system reliability and scale are not optional.
